wheels.title: Wheel
wheels.description: Pirelli tires used in Formula 1 cars are manufactured with different compounds and compounds. Tire temperature, pressure and wear directly affect performance. Aerodynamically, wheels are an important component that directs airflow. Carbon fiber rims provide lightness and durability.

hola.title: Cockpit
hola.description: The cockpit, designed for driver safety, is manufactured in accordance with FIA standards. The Halo system is a critical safety feature that has been mandatory since 2018. Inside the cockpit, driver position, viewing angle and ergonomics are optimized. The safety cell integrated with the monocoque structure protects the driver in collisions.

back_wings.title: Rear Wing
back_wings.description: The rear wing generates downforce at high speeds and maintains vehicle balance. The DRS (Drag Reduction System) opens on straight sections to reduce drag and increase passing speed. Wing angle and elements can be adjusted according to track conditions. It is constantly developed for aerodynamic efficiency.

front_wings.title: Front Wing
front_wings.description: The front wing is a critical aerodynamic component that controls airflow and generates downforce. Airflow is optimized with different elements and angles. Wing elements can be adjusted according to track conditions. Front wing design directly affects airflow throughout the vehicle and the performance of other aerodynamic components.

sidepod.title: Sidepod / Cooling
sidepod.description: Sidepods house the engine and power unit cooling systems. Air intakes, radiators and cooling channels are placed in an optimized manner. Aerodynamically, sidepod design directs airflow and contributes to downforce generation. Thermal management is critical for engine performance and reliability.

engine.title: Power Unit
engine.description: The modern Formula 1 power unit consists of a 1.6L V6 turbo engine, MGU-K (kinetic energy recovery), MGU-H (thermal energy recovery) and battery system. Total power reaches approximately 1000 horsepower. Hybrid technology optimizes performance while increasing fuel efficiency. Engine mapping and energy management are adjusted according to track conditions.
